Hi Satoshi (and Claire),

Thanks — appreciate the proposed time. Two quick scheduling flags I want to raise before sending a full invite:

- Golden Week: May 3–5 is Golden Week in Japan and many teams in APAC often have partial OOO. I want to be sure the people you expect will actually be available if we lock May 4.
- DST / timezone alignment: US colleagues are on PDT and EU attendees on CEST — the effective offsets mean a 09:00 JST demo lands mid-evening in the US the previous day. We should confirm global coverage windows so we don't lose a key attendee.

If you're OK, can we consider moving to either May 6 (Thu) 09:00 JST or May 7 (Fri) 11:00 JST so EU gets a more workable afternoon slot and US isn’t too late? Aditya/Soojin/Rafael — can you confirm availability windows below? I'll hold off on sending the invite until we have consensus.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Irene — quick availability notes and concrete options.

My calendar (PDT) — Thu May 6: 16:00-18:00 PDT (which is Fri May 7 08:00-10:00 JST). Fri May 7 at 13:00-15:00 PDT (Sat May 8 JST) is not ideal.
Soojin (APAC) — prefers after Golden Week so May 6 onward; she can staff 09:00–11:00 JST on May 6.
Rafael (EMEA) — CEST — can do May 6 at 17:00 CEST (which maps to 09:00 JST).

So the clean option that gives good coverage for all three regions is:
- May 6, 09:00 JST / May 5 16:00 CEST? Wait, check conversions carefully: 09:00 JST on May 6 = 02:00 CEST on May 6? (hold on)

Let me spell the conversions explicitly so we avoid DST traps:
- Option A: May 6, 09:00 JST = May 6 01:00 CEST / May 5 18:00 PDT — not great for EMEA.
- Option B: May 6, 17:00 CEST = May 6 00:00 JST (too late) — confusing.

Okay — better approach: pick a slot that centers EMEA midday, APAC late evening, US morning. Proposed workable slot: May 6 at 08:00 CEST / May 6 15:00 JST / May 6 07:00 PDT. Translating for you: that would be May 6, 15:00 JST. If Satoshi prefers morning JST for his team we can compromise on May 7 09:00 JST to make EMEA later afternoon and US evening earlier.

Satoshi / Claire — which is less painful for your side: Thu May 6 afternoon JST (15:00 JST) or Fri May 7 morning JST (09:00 JST)? Apologies for the messy math — DST offsets means the usual patterns flip a bit this window.

— Aditya

Best,
